newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-S. Africa airports firm to be privatised.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-S. Africa airports firm to be privatised.

text.p: South Africa cleared the runway on Monday for the partial privatisation of the state-owned Airports Company, appointing Deutsche Morgan Grenfell as its adviser and setting a target of March 1998 for a sale.

Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said the government planned to sell up to 49 percent of the company, which operates Africa's busiest airport in Johannesburg along with the airports in Cape Town and Durban and six regional airports.
"We expect that the process will be completed by March 1998 and then it is government's intention, hopefully within two years' time, to list the other 51 percent," Marahaj said.
Bankers bidding to advise on the sale had valued the total concern at around 2.5 billion rand ($550 million), he said.
The government expects 20 percent of the company to be sold to a foreign strategic equity partner which would form a consortium with local black business groups to take up to 49 percent in total.

Some 10 foreign companies had expressed strong interest in acquiring a stake in Airports Co, including BAA Plc, the Malaysia Airports Authority, and Schiphol, Vienna and Frankfurt airports, Maharaj said.

The sale of the airport operator is part of a continuing privatisation programme which is shifting to the South African transport sector following the sale of a 30 percent in telecommunications group Telkom to a U.S.-Malaysian consortium earlier this year.
The sale of 100 percent of domestic carrier Sun Air is now imminent, with binding bids due by next week.
Maharaj told Reuters after a news briefing that non-binding offers for the airline had ranged between 90 million and 140 million rand.

Richard Branson's Virgin Atlantic had been tipped as frontrunner to snap up Sun Air but it withdrew from the bidding last month in order to focus on the bigger prize of a stake in flag carrier South African Airways.

The government expects to sell an initial minority stake in SAA of up to 49 percent by the end of 1998. British Airways Plc and Deutsche Lufthansa AG are among other airlines to have expressed interest.
Also in the transport sector, Maharaj said the government aimed to privatise 100 percent of loss-making consignment distribution business PX and was reviewing the future of ports operator Portnet.
Maharaj said his ministry had been working closely with South Africa's influential trade unions who had accepted the need for restructuring in the sector.

"We've built a relationship with labour on a case-by-case approach and clearly spelled out general objectives. I think now we should be able to move much faster with other privatisations that come up in the transport sector," he said.
